audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere; 'his Q bite', 'his Pillar', 'his R' with no numbers.
audit.why: Chomp is a flat 3.5s at 300 range, Pillar of Ice 21s at rank 1 at 1000, Frozen Domain 18s, Subjugate 120s with the steal doubling over 4 seconds. The 3.5-second Chomp cadence is the whole rhythm of the lane and it was never stated.
audit.corrected: All four written into early, mid, late, spikes[3], breakdown.cooldowns and report[5].

audit.whatIsWrong: 'his R steals your armor and magic resist for a chunk of HP' understates and mis-times the effect, and Chomp's auto reset is never mentioned.
audit.why: Subjugate steals a share of resistances that doubles over the following 4 seconds — which makes it an opener, not a finisher, and the mirror reached the same conclusion from Trundle's side. Chomp is an auto-attack reset: the wind-up is the tell, not the cast, which is flagged in _missing-interactions for this pairing.
audit.corrected: Subjugate's 4-second doubling written into late, whys[6] and spikes[3]; Chomp named as a 3.5s auto reset with the wind-up as the step-back cue.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Use E to block his Q bite mid-trade so it neither damages you nor heals him as much' — Aegis Assault's direction is never stated.
audit.why: Riot: Pantheon is invulnerable to damage from the FRONT during the channel. Whether that also denies Chomp's attack-damage steal is not something the kit files answer, so the page should not imply a partial-heal-denial effect it cannot support.
audit.corrected: Rewritten as facing the shield at the bite; the vaguer 'heals him as much' clause dropped rather than restated.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Passive shield + Q poke wins level 1 outright'.
audit.why: Pantheon's passive is Mortal Will. The mirror flagged the same fiction on Trundle's page ('Aegis Assault is his E, not his passive').

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are yours. Your point-and-click W stun and Q poke beat his early game flat — he has no answer to a level-1 or level-2 all-in before his Q bite steals meaningful AD. Use E to block his Q bite mid-trade so it neither damages you nor heals him as much, then W-stun and Q-burst. Watch his Pillar (E): he'll drop it behind you to block your retreat or in front to wall your W, so commit your dash with an escape angle in mind.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are yours. Your point-and-click Shield Vault and Comet Spear beat his early game flat — he has no answer to a level-1 or level-2 all-in before Chomp steals meaningful AD. Chomp is a 3.5-second auto reset at 300 range, so the wind-up is your cue to step back, not the cast. Face Aegis Assault as it lands, then W-stun and burst. Pillar of Ice (21s at rank 1) is terrain: behind you it blocks the retreat, in front it walls your dash.

edits.before: Now it gets even. Through 4-5 you still poke with empowered Q and block his bite with E, but his sustain is online and your raw kill pressure dips — you won't solo-kill a Trundle who plays back behind Pillar. At 6, don't get tunneled trying to duel him; Grand Starfall is built for roams, so leap to a sidelane and convert your early lead into kills elsewhere while his immobile drain-tank can't follow.
edits.after: Now it gets even. notes: CHART, and this one is a genuine mirror conflict rather than a judgement call: my side had Pantheon winning both item stages while the same entry's late paragraph opens 'This is where he takes over and it's not close'. The mirror agent had already moved those two stages to Trundle on Trundle's page for the same reason. I matched them, so the two directions now agree. As with Tahm Kench, the full layer's phases[5].side and phases[6].side still read Pantheon and cannot be edited through this process — the applier rejects full-layer edits whose before string is under 12 characters, and every phases[].side value is shorter than that. The mechanical additions are Chomp's flat 3.5-second cadence (and its auto reset — the wind-up is the step-back cue, per _missing-interactions) and Subjugate's steal doubling over 4 seconds, which the mirror also established and which makes it an opener rather than a finisher. NOT ASSERTED: I dropped the claim that Aegis Assault makes Chomp heal him less. The kit files say nothing about whether the frontal block interacts with the attack-damage steal or the heal, and the mirror asserted it from the other side without a source, so I wrote only what Riot's text supports — the block soaks damage from the front.
